title: fix(cursor): repair the Cloud Agent bootstrap — drop unparseable ports field and fix the Node engine remediation
intent: Correct two defects inherited from PR #408 (CLOUD_AGENT_ENVIRONMENT_001) that each prevent a Cloud Agent from starting: (1) `.cursor/environment.json` declares `ports` as a list of bare integers, which Cursor's parser rejects; and (2) `.cursor/install.sh`'s Node engine-floor remediation calls bare `sudo npm ...`, which fails with `sudo: npm: command not found` because npm is not on root's secure PATH, so the client install never reaches `npm ci`. Fix both so the repository configuration installs cleanly on a fresh Cloud Agent.
behavior_change: Cursor Cloud Agent environments can be created and installed again. (1) The `ports` hint is removed; Cursor detects listening ports at runtime and offers forwarding without it. (2) install.sh now selects a Node that satisfies the client's declared engine floor without privilege escalation: it prefers an already-installed nvm Node that passes the repo's own check-node-engine.mjs, and only if none exists installs the exact pinned version 22.22.2 via user-level nvm; it then re-runs `npm run check:node` before `npm ci`. No repository build, test, CI, or runtime surface changes: `.cursor/*` is consumed only by Cursor's cloud-agent tooling. Both terminal definitions are byte-identical (api still binds 127.0.0.1:8010; client still runs Vite on 5173).

diff_articulation.what_changed: environment.json: removed `"ports": [8010, 5173]` and the trailing comma after `terminals` (unchanged since the original PR #411 commit 4afac01e). install.sh: replaced the client-node section — the old `if ! node scripts/check-node-engine.mjs; then sudo npm install --global n@10.2.0; sudo n 22; fi; npm run check:node; npm ci` — with a `select_supported_node` helper that (1) uses the active node if it already satisfies the floor, (2) otherwise prepends the bin of the newest already-installed nvm Node that passes the repo guard, (3) otherwise installs pinned Node 22.22.2 via user-level nvm; then `hash -r`, prints the resolved node/npm, runs `npm run check:node`, and `npm ci`. No `sudo npm` and no privilege escalation.
diff_articulation.why_removal_rather_than_a_reshape: The failing `ports` value is a list of integers and Cursor's parser wants a different shape the current docs do not specify; reshaping would be a guess. Cursor detects listening ports at runtime, so the field is not required for the 8010/5173 terminals.
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: No other change fixes these. Both defects are on origin/main at 7911dd3e (introduced by PR #408). PR #411 already removed `ports`; this amendment additionally repairs the install.sh Node remediation, which the removal alone did not address.
diff_articulation.what_did_not_change: `name`, `user`, `install`, and both `terminals` entries in environment.json are byte-identical. install.sh's system-dependency and Python-venv phases are unchanged. No application code, dependency manifest, lockfile, workflow, or governance artifact outside this manifest is involved. The Rosette containment work (CF2-ROSETTE-OUTPUT-CONTAINMENT-001) is untouched — no Rosette file appears in this branch.
diff_articulation.why_structural_extraction: No module extraction; the fix is localized to install.sh's client section as a self-contained shell function.

discovering_witness.summary: The install.sh Node defect was discovered by a FAILED environment validation, not by static review.
discovering_witness.detail: A branch environment validation ran `bash .cursor/install.sh` and it exited 1: `FATAL: Node 22.14.0 does not satisfy the client engine floor "^20.19.0 || >=22.22.2"` followed by `sudo: npm: command not found` (npm resides under /home/ubuntu/.nvm/... which is not on root's secure PATH). That validation ran on branch cursor/cf2-rosette-output-containment-600a @ 64555a3a using an owner-restricted transitional environment override and persisted dependencies, so it did NOT prove the repository configuration or a clean install; its only durable finding is this confirmed second PR #408 defect. This amendment fixes that defect and is validated by a clean disposable-agent witness on this branch instead.
discovering_witness.engine_floor_note: The declared floor was NOT relaxed. Vite happens to start under 22.14.0, but the fix honors the declared `engines.node` by selecting/installing a satisfying Node rather than weakening the guard.

commands_run: python json.load(.cursor/environment.json) -> parses; `ports` absent; terminals ['api','client'] preserved
bash .cursor/install.sh  # clean install #1 -> exit 0; selected node v22.22.2 (no sudo); npm run check:node passed; npm ci added 340 packages
start api + client terminals -> ports 8010 (uvicorn /health ok) and 5173 (Vite, HTTP 200) detected
verification.not_verified_locally: Whether Cursor's parser accepts the corrected environment.json is confirmed only by a Cloud Agent environment starting. The authoritative clean-install proof is the disposable-agent witness recorded on the PR; the local clean install above ran on the override VM (with the image's pre-existing nvm 22.22.2) and is a pre-check, not the independent witness.

files.intent: Remove the field Cursor's parser rejects.
files.behavior_change: Cloud agent environments build again; port forwarding falls back to Cursor's automatic detection.

files.intent: Select a Node satisfying the declared engine floor without `sudo npm`/privilege escalation, then run the repo guard and npm ci.
files.behavior_change: Client dependency install completes on the Cloud Agent base image instead of dying at `sudo: npm: command not found`.

findings: LOW: .cursor/* is consumed by an external tool whose schema this repository cannot validate in CI, so a malformed field or a broken install step passes every gate here and only fails when a Cloud Agent starts. That is how both PR #408 defects reached main with all checks green.

LOW: install.sh relies on nvm being present or reachable to install Node 22.22.2; on the current base image an nvm Node 22.22.2 is already installed, so the pinned-install fallback is exercised only if the image changes.
architecture_scan.acknowledgement_notes: External-tool configuration repair only. No repository build, test, CI, or runtime surface is affected, and the Rosette containment work is untouched.
